The bake reads his files first and this second; an entry marked scaffold is a placeholder that disappears the day his data names the same thing. Nothing here is a decision about the map — it is what lets every system and test run on his terrain today, and the bake's report says exactly what is still a proposal.

_yards: A yard is composed, not computed (G2–G4, 2026-09-21; it replaced a two-corner rectangle of tile-sized fence). Everything below is in HIS metres. A run lays one of his modules end marker to end marker from from_xz toward to_xz, as his own placement note says (extrémités à X = ±1 m, dupliquer pour prolonger); a run marked until: water stops on his bank. The gate is his portail_cour, its origin the middle of its 2.6 m passage: that tile stays open ground, warded, and a man stands on it. What each piece stops is what its own collision shapes cover. Two rules the bake enforces and reports: nothing stands in his river, and nothing crosses a road — a wall may run along a road's edge, and the one crossing is the gate.

yards._why: The furnace court, closed (docs/QUEST_CINDERWORKS.md §3), built from his own separation modules. It is the block his plan already draws: his work street (route ScierieAcierie) on the west, his charcoal lane (TraverseStockage, z 17) on the north, his finishing lane (TraverseFinition, z 56) beyond the south, and the river on the east with nothing built along it. Every run starts on a face of its neighbour and ends on one, or on his water; his own MuretMinerai_02 abuts the south wall from inside and his _03 lies a metre outside it, as the ore court he drew. The one way in is his portail_cour where his furnace traverse (TraverseFourneaux, z 32) leaves the street, between the two rows of furnaces, because that is the way a worker walks to them. Stone, not wood: his own walls at the works are soubassement_2m, and his wooden cloture_2m stands at the homes.
yards._rhythm: The corners are butt joints, one arm to the outer face and the other against its inner face, so nothing overlaps and nothing is notched. The gate's 3.26 m breaks the 2 m rhythm once, which is why the two corners are handed opposite ways: west 19.37→31.37 (6), the gate, west 34.63→48.63 (7). A run toward the water lays whole modules until the next would stand in a tile the sim calls water, so the module rhythm is chosen to land the last one in the last dry tile: the north run from x 255.2 ends 0.8 m short of the water tile at 286; the south run from 254.8 ends 1.2 m short of it at 280, and that last strip is closed by the wall's own reach (CatalogRules.REACH_M). Both are the 2 m tile's tax at a riverbank and are said here so nobody hunts for them.
